candidates.body_text: AI AND ML Samsung-led round values the French model maker at more than €21B Paris-based AI darling Mistral has raised €3 billion in Series D funding, giving it a post-money valuation of more than €21 billion. That makes it a minnow compared with OpenAI, but Mistral says it is the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company. Mistral is pitching itself as a sovereign alternative to US giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic. The company wrote : "During the first wave of generative AI, the central question was who could build the most powerful model. "Organizations and governments are now asking a different one: how to harness the power of AI for their mission-critical needs without surrendering control over the infrastructure and intelligence loop." Mistral's answer, unsurprisingly, is its own combination of open-weight models, infrastructure, and compute capacity. The pitch is aimed at organizations and public sector bodies increasingly wary of relying on overseas tech giants. The company's customers include aeronautics giant Airbus. Mistral has logged some impressive growth in its three years of existence. A year ago, it announced Series C funding of €1.7 billion at a post-money valuation of €11.7 billion. That round was led by ASML, with Nvidia and Andreessen Horowitz among the participants. candidates.body_text: September 8, 2026 Safety Funding grants for new research into AI and teen development OpenAI is committing $5 million to support independent research on how generative AI affects the lives and development of young people ages 13–17. Loading… Share What we’re funding Research priorities Research involving minors Application requirements Review criteria How to apply FAQ Apply now⁠ (opens in a new window) OpenAI is committing $5 million to support independent research on how generative AI affects the lives and development of young people ages 13–17. Generative AI is becoming part of how teens learn, create, and seek advice. Its effects are likely to be nuanced. They may depend on what teens use AI for, how they engage with it, their individual circumstances, and the support available from families, schools, communities, and technology providers. We want to build a stronger evidence base about the way teens use AI, as well as the impacts of AI on their lives, to inform development of AI products for teens and to help answer major questions facing policymakers and regulators. For example, we aim to deepen industry-wide understanding of the nuances across age and context, efficacy of safeguards and interventions, and the ways that evidence can inform implementation and evaluation. This program will fund independent research into the opportunities and challenges associated with AI use during adolescence, with a particular focus on teens’ social and emotional development.
